studies.title: Rhodiola rosea supplementation on sports performance: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
studies.abstract: The aim of this systematic review was to determine whether the supplementation with Rhodiola rosea (RR), an herb that has been used for centuries for its various properties, can have an effect on muscle damage and physical performance. The databases PubMed, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were used to find studies published until March 2023. Randomized controlled trials, healthy participants, and no use of other supplements. The search strategy was conducted by two independent reviewers, and specific information was extracted from the selected studies. Thirteen studies were included with 263 participants (198 men and 65 women between 18 and 65 years old). Two studies followed acute supplementation, 5 chronic, and 6 combined both. The results were heterogenous, having 11 studies with some positive effects, while 2 studies show no effect in variables such as rating of perceive exertion, heart rate, antioxidant capacity, blood lactate, creatine kinase, or C-reactive protein. Two limitations were found, firstly, the difference between supplementation and exercise protocols, and secondly, the existence of unclear or high risk of bias in most of the studies included. Acute supplementation with RR has a positive effect on endurance performance and rating of perceived exertion (RPE). Chronic supplementation has a positive effect on anaerobic exercise performance, but not endurance exercise performance. Chronic supplementation may positively impact muscle damage during exercise. However, more high-quality studies are needed to firmly establish the clinical efficacy of RR.

studies.title: Effects of Rhodiola Rosea Supplementation on Exercise and Sport: A Systematic Review.
studies.abstract: Rhodiola rosea (Golden Root Extract; RR) is an herbaceous perennial, which is native to high altitude areas, such as East Asia, Central Asia, Siberia, and North America. It has been studied for its positive pharmacological effects on health. However, only a handful of studies have evaluated the effects of RR as an exercise supplement for sport and physical activity. The aim of this study was to evaluate whether Rhodiola can be used as a supplement to improve human exercise ability. Studies were reviewed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines and conducted between August and November, 2021. Databases searched included Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, PubMed and East View Universal Database. Related terms were combined with keywords and MeSH subject headings using the corresponding Boolean operators: Rhodiola rosea, arctic root, roseroot, golden root, hongjingtian, and sports and exercise. A total of 10 papers were reviewed. Most of the studies reported that RR supplementation has a positive effect on athletic ability and sports performance, and no obvious adverse reactions were reported. Subjects taking RR showed a reduction in pain and muscle damage after exercise training, improved skeletal muscle damage, enhanced antioxidant capacity thereby reducing oxidative stress, reduced RPE scores, and improved athletic explosive power, but did not reduce the rating of perceived exertion (RPE) scores. RR appears to act as a safe and effective supplementation for sport and exercise.

studies.title: Combined Effects of Rhodiola Rosea and Caffeine Supplementation on Straight Punch Explosive Power in Untrained and Trained Boxing Volunteers: A Synergistic Appr
studies.abstract:
Objectives

This study aimed to investigate the effects of combined supplementation with Rhodiola rosea (RHO) and caffeine (CAF) on the explosive power and sustained output capacity of lead and rear straight punches in both untrained and trained volunteers, with a focus on potential synergistic effects.

Methods

randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design was employed, enrolling 96 participants (48 untrained, 48 trained). Participants were stratified and randomly assigned to the control (CTR), CAF, RHO, or CAF+RHO group. All subjects completed an 8-week standardized boxing training program (twice per week). Punch performance was assessed using professional boxing equipment and a biomechanical testing system, evaluating lead and rear straight punches, ground reaction force (GRF), and a 30 s continuous punching test.

Results

the CAF+RHO group showed significant improvements in both untrained and trained volunteers. Com-pared to the RHO group, this group demonstrated higher lead punch velocity, shorter bi-lateral peak force time during rear punches, and more punches in the 30 s test (p < 0.05). Compared to the CAF group, the CAF+RHO group exhibited greater rear punch force, higher bilateral peak force during lead punches, increased forefoot peak force in rear punches, and improved 30 s power output (p < 0.05). The CAF+RHO group also outperformed the CTR group across all parameters (p < 0.05).

Conclusions

Combined supple mentation with CAF and RHO significantly enhances both explosive power and sustained output in boxing performance. This may result from improved energy metabolism efficiency and neuromuscular coordination, providing a promising nutritional strategy for high-intensity intermittent exercise.

studies.title: The Effects of Rhodiola rosea L. Extract on Anxiety, Stress, Cognition and Other Mood Symptoms.
studies.abstract: This trial evaluated the impact of a Rhodiola rosea L. extract on self-reported anxiety, stress, cognition, and other mood symptoms. Eighty mildly anxious participants were randomized into two different groups of either Rhodiola rosea L (2 × 200 mg dose Vitano®, 1 tablet taken before breakfast and 1tablet before lunch) or a control condition (no treatment). Self-report measures and cognitive tests were completed at four testing sessions over a period of 14 days. Relative to the controls, the experimental group demonstrated a significant reduction in self-reported, anxiety, stress, anger, confusion and depression at 14 days and a significant improvements in total mood. No relevant differences in cognitive performance between the groups were observed. Rhodiola rosea L (Vitano®) presented a favourable safety tolerability profile. Although this was a non-placebo controlled trial, it is unlikely that the findings were the result of placebo effects as changes appeared gradual and were specific to certain psychological measures. However, we cannot determine a causal relationship; further investigations are recommended to support the effects of Rhodiola rosea L. extract on stress related symptoms.

studies.title: Rhodiola rosea L. roots powder strongly reduces anxiety and corticosterone level induced by chronic stress in a murine model.
studies.abstract: Chronic stress disrupts physiological and psychological homeostasis, yet effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. This study investigated the adaptogenic effects of Rhodiola rosea root powder (standardized to 3% salidroside) on stress-induced behavioral and physiological changes in a murine model of chronic mild stress. Female C57BL/6 mice were exposed to a 19-day chronic mild stress protocol and received daily oral supplementation of Rhodiola rosea root powder, administered in gummies to ensure accurate and stress-free intake, or a placebo. At the end of the experiment, behavioral outcomes were assessed using the Elevated Plus Maze (EPM) and Open Field (OF) tests. Compared with stressed controls, stressed treated mice demonstrated significant improvements. In the EPM, treated mice showed significantly higher locomotor activity (greater distance and speed), with more open-arm entries and time, as well as increased head dips, indicating reduced anxiety and enhanced exploration. In the OF test, they also displayed greater locomotion and more center-zone entries, both reaching statistical significance and supporting reduced anxiety-like behavior. These behavioral improvements were accompanied by a significant reduction in serum corticosterone levels, indicating modulation of the physiological stress response. Together, the findings support the anxiolytic and adaptogenic properties of Rhodiola rosea root powder and highlight its potential as a natural intervention for managing chronic stress. Future studies should investigate the long-term efficacy and mechanisms of its bioactive compounds in stress resilience and mental health.

studies.title: Amelioration of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by Rhodiola rosea, a natural adaptogen.
studies.abstract: Adaptogens are stress-response modifiers which have been considered to exert important influences on cytokines activities and immune response. Here, we investigated the effects of Rhodiola rosea (R. rosea), a natural adaptogen on the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), an animal model of multiple sclerosis (MS). We found that R. rosea alleviated the severity of EAE as evaluated by clinical and histopathology scores. R. rosea decreased IL-6, sIL-6R, IFN-γ and IL-17A in both serum and splenocytes supernatants while increased IL-4 in splenocytes supernatants of EAE mice. R. rosea also modulated the T cell response by inhibiting Th1 and Th17 cells, restoring Treg cells, combining with regulated Th17/Th1, Th17/Th2 and Th17/Treg ratios in the spleen, inguinal lymph nodes, brain and spinal cord of EAE mice. Furthermore, R. rosea regulated the expression of JAK1, JAK2, STAT3 and RORγt in the spinal cord of EAE mice. Together, our findings suggested the adaptogenic effects of R. rosea on EAE, which may help to deepen the understanding of potential therapeutic values of traditional Chinese medicines for autoimmune diseases of CNS.

studies.title: Evaluation of Rhodiola rosea supplementation on skeletal muscle damage and inflammation in runners following a competitive marathon.
studies.abstract: Adaptogens modulate intracellular signaling and increase expression of heat shock protein 72 (HSP72). Rhodiola rosea (RR) is a medicinal plant with demonstrated adaptogenic properties. The purpose of this study was to measure the influence of RR supplementation on exercise-induced muscle damage, delayed onset of muscle soreness (DOMS), plasma cytokines, and extracellular HSP72 (eHSP72) in experienced runners completing a marathon. Experienced marathon runners were randomized to RR (n=24, 6 female, 18 male) or placebo (n=24, 7 female, 17 male) groups and under double-blinded conditions ingested 600mg/day RR extract or placebo for 30days prior to, the day of, and seven days post-marathon. Blood samples were collected, and vertical jump and DOMS assessed the day before, 15min post- and 1.5h post-marathon. DOMS was also assessed for seven days post-marathon. Marathon race performance did not differ between RR and placebo groups (3.87±0.12h and 3.93±0.12h, respectively, p=0.722). Vertical jump decreased post-marathon (time effect, p<0.001) with no difference between groups (interaction effect, p=0.673). Post-marathon DOMS increased significantly (p<0.001) but the pattern of change did not differ between groups (p=0.700). Myoglobin (Mb), creatine phosphokinase (CPK), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, IL-10, monocyte chemotactic protein-1 (MCP-1), granulocyte-colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF), C-reactive protein (CRP), and eHSP72 all increased post-marathon (all p<0.001), with no group differences over time (all p>0.300). In conclusion, RR supplementation (600mg/day) for 30days before running a marathon did not attenuate the post-marathon decrease in muscle function, or increases in muscle damage, DOMS, eHSP72, or plasma cytokines in experienced runners.

studies.title: The clinical efficacy and mechanism of Rhodiola rosea in treating rheumatoid arthritis in high-altitude areas by regulating the HIF-1α signaling pathway.
studies.abstract:
Objective

To evaluate the clinical efficacy of Rhodiola rosea in high-altitude rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients and to investigate, in vitro, whether its anti-inflammatory mechanism is mediated by the HIF-1α signaling pathway.

Methods

This study adopted a retrospective analysis. Patients with RA in high-altitude areas were divided into the Rhodiola rosea treatment group (74 cases) and the conventional treatment group (86 cases). Baseline data, disease activity score (DAS28), inflammatory factors (CRP, ESR, TNF-α, and IL-6), serum HIF-1α levels, imaging data, and adverse reaction monitoring data were collected to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of Rhodiola rosea. Human synovial cells (HFLS-RA) were used for in vitro experiments to establish a hypoxic model. Using CCK-8, qRT-PCR, Western Blot, and gene overexpression techniques, the molecular mechanism was further explored.

Results

The Rhodiola rosea treatment group showed significantly better improvements in DAS28, CRP, ESR, TNF-α, and IL-6 compared to the conventional treatment group (p < 0.05). Imaging assessment showed greater reductions in synovial thickness and blood-flow signals in the knee and metacarpophalangeal joints in the Rhodiola rosea group than in the conventional treatment group. The serum HIF-1α level in the Rhodiola rosea group was significantly lower, and the incidence of adverse reactions (18.92%) was significantly lower than that of the conventional treatment group (34.88%), without any serious adverse events. The in vitro experiments showed that Rhodiola rosea injection (RRI) reduced hypoxia-induced expression of HIF-1α and its downstream factors MMP-3, VEGF, COX-2, and ICAM-1.

Conclusion

Rhodiola rosea was associated with improved disease activity and inflammatory markers in high-altitude RA patients, with a favorable safety profile. The in vitro findings suggest that inhibition of HIF-1α signaling may be one potential mechanism, although prospective and translational validation is still required.

studies.title: Research on the Anti-Fatigue Effects and Mechanisms of Arecoline in Sleep-Deprived Mice.
studies.abstract: The betel nut is one of the most widely consumed addictive substances in the world after nicotine, ethanol, and caffeine. Arecoline is an active ingredient from the areca nut. It has many pharmacological effects and can affect the central nervous system. In this study, we found that arecoline can relieve fatigue behavior. This research aims to estimate the anti-fatigue effects of arecoline and explore its underlying mechanisms using a murine model of central fatigue precipitated by sleep deprivation (SD). Seventy-two male C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to six groups: a control group, an SD-induced fatigue model group, a group that received Rhodiola Rosea capsules (2.5 mg/kg), and three arecoline groups, which were administered at low, medium, and high doses (10, 20, and 40 mg/kg, respectively). Following 28 days of continuous administrations, the effects of arecoline on mouse fatigue-related behaviors were assessed by behavioral tests, including grip strength, rotarod performance, and weight-bearing swimming endurance. The release levels of the related biochemical markers were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs). Western blotting was employed to quantify the expression levels of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor (Nrf2), Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1), heme oxygenase 1 (HO-1), sequestosome-1 (p62), and NADPH quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1) in the gastrocnemius muscle. Arecoline administration notably enhanced grip strength, delayed the onset of fatigue as evidenced by extended latencies in rotarod tests, and increased the duration of weight-bearing swimming in mice. In the elevated plus maze, arecoline obviously decreased both the number of entries and the total distance traveled in the open arms. Arecoline markedly decreased the contents of creatine kinase, blood urea nitrogen, lactate dehydrogenase, triglycerides, and cholesterol in the serum, while it elevated the levels of total testosterone, lactate dehydrogenase, and immunoglobulin G. Furthermore, it significantly increased the activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and glutathione peroxidase in the gastrocnemius muscle, reduced malondialdehyde levels, augmented hippocampal SOD and CAT activity, and elevated glycogen stores in both liver and muscle tissues. Neurotransmitter levels showed significant increases, cytokine levels were markedly reduced, and the expressions of Nrf2, Keap1, NQO1, p62, and HO-1 in brain tissues were significantly upregulated. This study demonstrates that arecoline has anti-fatigue activity, and the specific mechanisms are associated with elevating glucose and lipid metabolism levels, relieving oxidative stress damage, inhibiting neuroinflammatory response, and regulating neurotransmitter levels and the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway. The research provides a new direction for arecoline's potential in preventing and improving fatigue.

studies.title: The impact of Rhodiola rosea on biomarkers of diabetes, inflammation, and microbiota in a leptin receptor-knockout mouse model.
studies.abstract: Type 2 diabetes is the most prevalent endocrine disease in the world, and recently the gut microbiota have become a potential target for its management. Recent studies have illustrated that this disease may predispose individuals to certain microbiome compositions, and treatments like metformin have been shown to change gut microbiota and their associated metabolic pathways. However, given the limitations and side effects associated with pharmaceuticals currently being used for therapy of diabetes, there is a significant need for alternative treatments. In this study, we investigated the effects of a root extract from Rhodiola rosea in a Leptin receptor knockout (db/db) mouse model of type 2 diabetes. Our previous work showed that Rhodiola rosea had anti-inflammatory and gut microbiome-modulating properties, while extending lifespan in several animal models. In this study, treatment with Rhodiola rosea improved fasting blood glucose levels, altered the response to exogenous insulin, and decreased circulating lipopolysaccharide and hepatic C-reactive protein transcript levels. We hypothesize that these changes may in part reflect the modulation of the microbiota, resulting in improved gut barrier integrity and decreasing the translocation of inflammatory biomolecules into the bloodstream. These findings indicate that Rhodiola rosea is an attractive candidate for further research in the management of type 2 diabetes.

studies.title: Rhodiola rosea L. improved intestinal digestive enzyme activities, inflammatory response, barrier and microbiota dysbiosis in Lateolabrax maculatus juveniles fe
studies.abstract: A 56-d feeding trial was conducted to evaluate the influences of Rhodiola rosea L. on digestive enzyme activities, intestinal barrier, inflammatory response, and microbiota dysbiosis in Lateolabrax maculatus juveniles (9.37 ± 0.03 g) fed with high-carbohydrate diets. Six diets were designed: a control diet (20% corn starch, Control), high-carbohydrate diet (30% corn starch, HC1), and four high-carbohydrate diets supplemented with Rhodiola rosea L. at 30, 60, 90 and 120 mg/kg (HC2, HC3, HC4 and HC5, respectively). Compared with the control group, the HC1 diet remarkably increased α-amylase, lipase, and chymotrypsin activities in the intestine (p < 0.05), as well as the mRNA levels of Claudin-15, NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-8 (p < 0.05) and the relative abundance of Proteobacteria and Photobacterium in the intestine, which belong to the phylum and genus level, respectively. But the opposite trend was found in muscular thickness and villus lengths (p < 0.05), the mRNA levels of Occludin, ZO-1, and TGF-β (p < 0.05), at the level of phylum and genus level in the HC1 group, and the relative abundance of Firmicutes, Bacteroidetes, and Bacillus in the intestine compared with the control group. Intestinal chymotrypsin activity was significantly higher in the HC3 group and intestinal muscular thickness and villus lengths were also significantly higher in the HC2, HC3, HC4, and HC5 groups compared to the HC1 group (p < 0.05). In addition, Occludin mRNA expression in the intestine was significantly increased in the HC2, HC4, and HC5 groups compared to the HC1 group. ZO-1 and TGF-β mRNA expression in the intestine were significantly increased in the HC2, HC3, HC4, and HC5 groups compared to the HC1 group (p < 0.05). At the phylum level, the relative abundance of Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes was higher in the intestine in the HC2, HC3, HC4, and HC5 groups than that in the HC1 group. On the contrary, intestinal lipase and chymotrypsin activities were significantly decreased in the HC2 group compared to the HC1 group, respectively (p < 0.05). The Claudin-15, NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-8 mRNA expression in the intestine were significantly decreased in the HC2, HC3, HC4, and HC5 groups compared to the HC1 group (p < 0.05). Besides, at the genus level, compared to the HC1 group, the relative abundance of Photobacterium in the intestine and the diversity of the intestinal microbiota in the HC2, HC3, HC4, and HC5 groups were all decreased. In conclusion, these results demonstrated that the addition of Rhodiola rosea L. in high-carbohydrate diets can improve intestinal digestive enzyme activities, inflammatory response and intestinal barrier-related gene expression, and microbiota dysbiosis in L. maculatus. The suitable supplemental level of Rhodiola rosea L. in high-carbohydrate diets of L. maculatus is 60 mg/kg.

studies.title: Can Rhodiola rosea supplementation mitigate digital eye strain? A triple-blinded placebo-controlled study.
studies.abstract: This study aimed to assess the impact of Rhodiola rosea (RR) supplementation on the dynamics of the accommodative response and digital eye strain (DES) symptoms following 30-min visual tasks with different levels of cognitive demand. Eighteen young adults (mean age ± SD: 24.6 ± 4.0 years) participated in this placebo-controlled, triple-blind, balanced crossover study. Participants completed four sessions separated by 1 week in a randomised order. The sessions differed in the supplement (RR or placebo) and cognitive demand of the visual task (Stroop test or control video). The supplementation consisted of 1200 mg of RR or placebo per day for 4 days (two 300 mg capsules every 12 h) and a washout period of 3 days was allowed before the subsequent condition. The lag and variability of the accommodative response were measured at 500, 40 and 20 cm using an open-field autorefractor, and DES symptoms were assessed using a 10-item questionnaire. RR supplementation caused a reduction in the variability of accommodation (p = 0.007) and the perceived levels of 'Blurred vision when looking into the distance at the end of the near task' (p = 0.009). However, the lag of accommodation (p = 0.15) and the remainder of the DES symptoms were unaffected by the ingestion of RR (p > 0.05 in all cases). The reduction in the variability of accommodation after RR intake was observed at 40 and 20 cm (p-values <0.001 and 0.04, respectively), but not at far distance (500 cm, p = 0.40). These findings show that RR supplementation (1200 mg/day for 4 days) produced a reduction in the variability of accommodation and one of the assessed DES symptoms, suggesting that it could be considered as a potential strategy to prevent or manage DES. However, further research is needed to determine its clinical relevance and optimise dosage and timing.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A plant extract traditionally used in Eastern medicine; studied for endurance and stress resilience.
explanation.what_it_is: Rhodiola rosea is an herb native to cold, mountainous regions of Eastern Europe and Asia. The supplement is made from extracts of its root, which contains compounds called rosavins and salidroside that are thought to be bioactive. People typically take it as a capsule or liquid extract.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Likely helps cells produce energy and manage stress hormones; exact pathways in humans not fully mapped.
explanation.how_it_works: Rhodiola appears to work through several mechanisms. First, it may help your cells produce and use ATP (the molecule they burn for quick energy) more efficiently, which could support endurance during exercise. Second, it seems to influence stress hormones — in animal studies, it reduced corticosterone (a hormone released during chronic stress) and calmed anxiety-related brain activity. Third, it shows anti-inflammatory effects in animal models, dampening immune signals that drive inflammation. However, the precise molecular targets in humans are not yet fully established from the studies retrieved; most detailed mechanism work comes from animal and cell research.
explanation.safety_line: Short-term use reported as well-tolerated; long-term and drug-interaction data remain limited.
explanation.safety_detail: The human trials retrieved reported no major safety concerns in participants over the study periods (typically weeks to a few months of use). However, these studies are limited in duration and do not cover all populations — for instance, the evidence excludes pregnant and breastfeeding women, children, and people with kidney or liver disease. No adequately powered studies retrieved examined interactions with common medications.
safety_bullets: No interaction data with common medications or supplements — untested whether it affects drug metabolism or efficacy
Excluded from nearly all trials: pregnancy, breastfeeding, under age 18, kidney/liver disease — effects unknown in these groups
Long-term safety (>6 months) has not been adequately studied in the records retrieved
explanation.chem_meaning: Rhodiola extracts are water- and fat-soluble, meaning they dissolve in both aqueous and lipid environments in the body; this mixed solubility helps them cross cell membranes and reach intracellular targets. The active compounds (rosavins, salidroside) are moderate-sized organic molecules, neither extremely small nor large, which favours oral absorption and distribution through the bloodstream.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews (2022, 2023, 2025) involving approximately 369 participants total found that rhodiola supplementation showed improvements in exercise-related outcomes, including one 2025 study of 96 untrained individuals showing enhanced punching explosive power when combined with caffeine. The 2023 systematic review of 263 participants across randomized controlled trials concluded there were measurable benefits on sports performance metrics.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Evidence comes from multiple human trials with reasonable sample sizes (263–369 participants across studies), but the total evidence base is modest (3 studies) and precision limits exist — the true effect size may vary. Moderate grade reflects genuine human evidence balanced against these constraints.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: One human RCT (2015) reported effects of rhodiola extract on anxiety and stress measures in participants. Two animal studies (2020, 2026) found that rhodiola reduced anxiety-like behaviour and lowered corticosterone (a stress hormone) in rodent models of chronic stress and neuroinflammation.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only one human study addresses this outcome, so consistency across independent human trials cannot be assessed. The animal data are supportive but do not confirm effects in people. Emerging reflects promising preliminary evidence rather than established human efficacy.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human studies (a 2022 systematic review of 10 participants and a 2014 RCT of 24 runners) examined inflammation markers and found reductions in inflammatory biomarkers following rhodiola supplementation and exercise. Four animal studies (2022, 2024, 2024, 2026) found rhodiola reduced inflammatory cytokines, improved intestinal barrier function, and ameliorated inflammation in models of rheumatoid arthritis and metabolic disease.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Human evidence exists (2 studies, 34 verified participants) with supportive animal data, but sample sizes are small and only one systematic review synthesis is available in the records — independent replication is lacking. Moderate reflects real human signal balanced against modest precision.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human RCTs (2015, 2025) examined cognition and related outcomes: the 2015 study measured cognitive function as part of a broader mood assessment, and the 2025 triple-blinded study of 96+ participants tested whether rhodiola could mitigate digital eye strain and associated cognitive burden.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Both studies are human RCTs, but exact sample sizes could not be verified from abstracts alone, and the evidence base is small (n=2). Moderate reflects human data present but imprecision and small sample concern.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence for rhodiola is dominated by human randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews, particularly for exercise performance and cognition. For stress/anxiety and inflammation, human studies are few (1–2 per outcome), but animal models provide supporting mechanistic data. Most retrieved studies are recent (2014–2026), and total human participant numbers are modest (~369 for exercise, ~34–96 for others). This means there is real human evidence, but it is not yet extensive or uniformly precise — confidence is moderate across most outcomes.
explanation.open_questions: The records retrieved show limited data in some populations: adolescents and older adults appear underrepresented, and long-term outcomes (beyond 2–3 months) are sparse. Whether benefits persist with continuous use or fade over time is unclear from these studies. Additionally, the mechanism by which rhodiola affects human cognition, stress hormones, and inflammation is still being mapped — animal studies provide clues, but direct mechanistic confirmation in people is lacking. Interaction with psychiatric medications and effect size in clinical anxiety or depression (beyond stress resilience) remain untested in the sample retrieved.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base is thin and heavily reliant on animal studies for mechanistic claims; human trials are few, underpowered, and lack transparent sample size reporting, making it impossible to assess precision for most outcomes.

concerns.issue: Majority animal evidence, limited human replication
concerns.detail: Across six inflammation studies, four are animal models with no independent human replication of the finding. For stress/anxiety (3 total studies), only one is human; the remaining two are animal. This creates a large translational gap: animal models of anxiety or inflammation do not reliably predict human clinical benefit. Without multiple independent human RCTs, animal findings remain mechanistic hypotheses, not evidence of efficacy.

concerns.issue: Pervasive sample size opacity in human trials
concerns.detail: For cognition (2 human RCTs) and stress/anxiety (1 human RCT), abstracts do not report sample sizes at all—the engine explicitly notes 'sample sizes could not be verified.' For inflammation, only 2 of 6 studies report n (10 and 24), leaving 4 studies' power entirely unknown. This opacity prevents assessment of whether observed effects reflect real signals or sampling noise, and prevents readers from gauging whether results are reproducible.

concerns.issue: Unstable effect estimates from small verified samples
concerns.detail: Exercise performance (the best-studied outcome) rests on only ~369 participants across 3 studies, with one trial enrolling just 10 people. The engine flags this as 'modest' and notes the estimate 'may be unstable.' For inflammation, only 34 verified participants across 2 human studies underpin a Moderate grade. A single large or outlier trial could shift the pooled direction; conversely, any summary estimate is highly sensitive to which studies happened to be retrieved.

concerns.issue: No pooled effect extractable, precluding meta-analytic precision
concerns.detail: Across all four outcomes, the engine reports 'none extractable' for pooled effect. This means the retrieved abstracts do not provide sufficient detail (effect sizes, confidence intervals, or raw data) to conduct or verify a meta-analysis. Grades are thus based on qualitative assessment of study design and sample size, not quantitative synthesis—a lower standard of evidence than a robust meta-analysis with sensitivity analysis.

concerns.issue: Single systematic review underpins two separate outcome grades
concerns.detail: The 2022 systematic review (n=10) appears in both exercise performance and inflammation evidence bases. A single review, even if high-quality, cannot independently verify consistency across outcomes. If that review has methodological flaws or publication bias, both grades are compromised. The 2023 exercise review (n=263) is also a systematic review, not an independent RCT, so human exercise evidence rests on secondary synthesis of primary trials of unknown individual quality.

appraisal.mechanism_check: The animal studies suggest Rhodiola may modulate inflammatory markers (cytokines, corticosterone) and anti-fatigue pathways, which plausibly connects to reduced anxiety and improved exercise resilience. However, there is a substantial leap from rodent biomarker changes to human clinical outcomes: human stress/anxiety evidence is a single 2015 RCT (sample size unknown), and exercise performance evidence conflates systematic reviews with one small 2025 RCT. The mechanism is biologically coherent, but the human clinical evidence is too sparse and opaque to confirm whether the pathway translates to meaningful human benefit.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that 4 of 6 inflammation studies and 2 of 3 stress/anxiety studies are animal models, which frequently fail to translate to human efficacy. The single human RCT on stress/anxiety (2015) is 11 years old, unpowered by modern standards, and has no reported sample size in the abstract—it may be a small pilot. For exercise performance, the evidence relies on systematic reviews (secondary synthesis, not independent trials) and a single 2025 RCT of 96 participants with an untested combination (Rhodiola + caffeine), making it unclear which agent, if any, is responsible. Absence of pooled effect estimates across all outcomes suggests heterogeneity or low-quality primary data, consistent with a null or trivial true effect masked by publication bias.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Preregistered, adequately powered (n≥150 per arm) RCTs in humans on single outcomes (e.g., VO₂max in endurance athletes, cortisol in clinical anxiety) with transparent sample size reporting, effect sizes, and confidence intervals would allow proper meta-analytic synthesis and detection of publication bias. A direct human replication of the 2015 stress/anxiety trial with modern methodology would establish whether that finding is reproducible.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un extracto de planta utilizado tradicionalmente en la medicina oriental; estudiado por su capacidad de resistencia y resiliencia ante el estrés.
explanation_es.what_it_is: Rhodiola rosea es una hierba nativa de regiones frías y montañosas de Europa Oriental y Asia. El suplemento se elabora a partir de extractos de su raíz, que contiene compuestos llamados rosavinas y salidrosida que se cree que son bioactivos. Las personas generalmente la toman en forma de cápsula o extracto líquido.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Probablemente ayuda a las células a producir energía y regular las hormonas del estrés; las vías exactas en humanos aún no se han mapeado completamente.
explanation_es.how_it_works: Rhodiola parece actuar a través de varios mecanismos. Primero, puede ayudar a que tus células produzcan y utilicen ATP (la molécula que queman para obtener energía rápida) de manera más eficiente, lo que podría respaldar la resistencia durante el ejercicio. Segundo, parece influir en las hormonas del estrés — en estudios en animales, redujo la corticosterona (una hormona liberada durante el estrés crónico) y calmó la actividad cerebral relacionada con la ansiedad. Tercero, muestra efectos antiinflamatorios en modelos animales, atenuando las señales inmunológicas que impulsan la inflamación. Sin embargo, los objetivos moleculares precisos en humanos aún no se han establecido completamente a partir de los estudios recuperados; la mayoría del trabajo detallado sobre mecanismos proviene de investigación en animales y células.
explanation_es.safety_line: El uso a corto plazo se reporta como bien tolerado; los datos sobre uso a largo plazo e interacciones farmacológicas siguen siendo limitados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos en humanos recuperados no reportaron preocupaciones de seguridad importantes en los participantes durante los períodos de estudio (típicamente semanas a algunos meses de uso). Sin embargo, estos estudios son limitados en duración y no cubren todas las poblaciones — por ejemplo, la evidencia excluye a mujeres embarazadas y en lactancia, niños y personas con enfermedad renal o hepática. Ningún estudio recuperado con poder estadístico adecuado examinó interacciones con medicamentos comunes.
safety_bullets: Sin datos de interacción con medicamentos comunes o suplementos — no probado si afecta el metabolismo de fármacos o su eficacia
Excluida de casi todos los ensayos: embarazo, lactancia, menores de 18 años, enfermedad renal/hepática — los efectos son desconocidos en estos grupos
La seguridad a largo plazo (>6 meses) no ha sido estudiada adecuadamente en los registros recuperados
explanation_es.chem_meaning: Los extractos de Rhodiola son solubles en agua y lípidos, lo que significa que se disuelven tanto en ambientes acuosos como lipídicos en el cuerpo; esta solubilidad mixta les ayuda a cruzar las membranas celulares y llegar a objetivos intracelulares. Los compuestos activos (rosavinas, salidrosida) son moléculas orgánicas de tamaño moderado, ni extremadamente pequeñas ni grandes, lo que favorece la absorción oral y la distribución a través del torrente sanguíneo.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ensayos controlados aleatorios y revisiones sistemáticas (2022, 2023, 2025) que involucraron aproximadamente 369 participantes en total encontraron que la suplementación con rhodiola mostró mejoras en resultados relacionados con el ejercicio, incluyendo un estudio de 2025 de 96 individuos sin entrenamiento que mostró mayor potencia explosiva en puñetazos cuando se combinó con cafeína. La revisión sistemática de 2023 de 263 participantes en ensayos controlados aleatorios concluyó que había beneficios medibles en métricas de rendimiento deportivo.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia proviene de múltiples ensayos en humanos con tamaños de muestra razonables (263–369 participantes entre estudios), pero la base de evidencia total es modesta (3 estudios) y existen limitaciones de precisión — el verdadero tamaño del efecto puede variar. La calificación moderada refleja evidencia humana genuina equilibrada con estas limitaciones.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un ensayo aleatorio controlado en humanos (2015) reportó efectos del extracto de rhodiola en medidas de ansiedad y estrés en participantes. Dos estudios en animales (2020, 2026) encontraron que rhodiola redujo el comportamiento similar a la ansiedad y disminuyó la corticosterona (una hormona del estrés) en modelos de roedores de estrés crónico e inflamación neurológica.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo un estudio en humanos aborda este resultado, por lo que no se puede evaluar la consistencia entre ensayos independientes en humanos. Los datos en animales son respaldadores pero no confirman efectos en personas. Emergente refleja evidencia preliminar prometedora en lugar de eficacia humana establecida.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos estudios en humanos (una revisión sistemática de 2022 de 10 participantes y un ensayo aleatorio controlado de 2014 de 24 corredores) examinaron marcadores de inflamación y encontraron reducciones en biomarcadores inflamatorios tras la suplementación con rhodiola y ejercicio. Cuatro estudios en animales (2022, 2024, 2024, 2026) encontraron que rhodiola redujo citoquinas inflamatorias, mejoró la función de la barrera intestinal y amelioró la inflamación en modelos de artritis reumatoide y enfermedad metabólica.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Existe evidencia en humanos (2 estudios, 34 participantes verificados) con datos en animales respaldadores, pero los tamaños de muestra son pequeños y solo una síntesis de revisión sistemática está disponible en los registros — falta replicación independiente. Moderada refleja una señal real en humanos equilibrada con precisión modesta.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos ensayos aleatorios controlados en humanos (2015, 2025) examinaron cognición y resultados relacionados: el estudio de 2015 midió la función cognitiva como parte de una evaluación más amplia del estado de ánimo, y el estudio triple ciego de 2025 de 96+ participantes evaluó si rhodiola podría mitigar la fatiga ocular digital y la carga cognitiva asociada.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Ambos estudios son ensayos aleatorios controlados en humanos, pero los tamaños exactos de muestra no pudieron verificarse solo desde los resúmenes, y la base de evidencia es pequeña (n=2). Moderada refleja que hay datos en humanos presentes pero con preocupaciones de imprecisión y tamaño de muestra pequeño.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia para rhodiola está dominada por ensayos controlados aleatorios en humanos y revisiones sistemáticas, particularmente para rendimiento del ejercicio y cognición. Para estrés/ansiedad e inflamación, hay pocos estudios en humanos (1–2 por resultado), pero los modelos en animales proporcionan datos mecanísticos respaldadores. La mayoría de los estudios recuperados son recientes (2014–2026), y el número total de participantes humanos es modesto (~369 para ejercicio, ~34–96 para otros). Esto significa que hay evidencia humana real, pero aún no es extensa ni uniformemente precisa — la confianza es moderada en la mayoría de los resultados.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados muestran datos limitados en algunas poblaciones: adolescentes y adultos mayores parecen estar subrepresentados, y los resultados a largo plazo (más allá de 2–3 meses) son escasos. Si los beneficios persisten con el uso continuo o se desvanecen con el tiempo no está claro a partir de estos estudios. Además, el mecanismo por el cual rhodiola afecta la cognición, las hormonas del estrés y la inflamación en humanos aún se está mapeando — los estudios en animales proporcionan pistas, pero la confirmación mecanística directa en personas es limitada. La interacción con medicamentos psiquiátricos y el tamaño del efecto en ansiedad o depresión clínica (más allá de la resiliencia al estrés) permanecen sin probar en la muestra recuperada.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia es escasa y depende en gran medida de estudios en animales para afirmaciones mecanicistas; los ensayos en humanos son pocos, insuficientemente potenciados y carecen de informes transparentes del tamaño de muestra, lo que hace imposible evaluar la precisión para la mayoría de los resultados.

concerns.issue: Mayoría de evidencia en animales, replicación humana limitada
concerns.detail: En seis estudios de inflamación, cuatro son modelos animales sin replicación humana independiente del hallazgo. Para estrés/ansiedad (3 estudios totales), solo uno es en humanos; los dos restantes son en animales. Esto crea una brecha traslacional considerable: los modelos animales de ansiedad o inflamación no predicen de manera confiable el beneficio clínico humano. Sin múltiples ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos independientes, los hallazgos en animales siguen siendo hipótesis mecanicistas, no evidencia de eficacia.

concerns.issue: Opacidad generalizada del tamaño de muestra en ensayos humanos
concerns.detail: Para cognición (2 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos) y estrés/ansiedad (1 ensayo clínico aleatorizado en humanos), los resúmenes no reportan tamaños de muestra en absoluto—el motor explícitamente señala que 'no se pudieron verificar los tamaños de muestra.' Para inflamación, solo 2 de 6 estudios reportan n (10 y 24), dejando la potencia de 4 estudios completamente desconocida. Esta opacidad impide evaluar si los efectos observados reflejan señales reales o ruido de muestreo, y evita que los lectores evalúen si los resultados son reproducibles.

concerns.issue: Estimaciones de efectos inestables de muestras pequeñas verificadas
concerns.detail: El desempeño del ejercicio (el resultado mejor estudiado) se basa en solo ~369 participantes en 3 estudios, con un ensayo que inscribió solo 10 personas. El motor lo marca como 'modesto' y señala que la estimación 'podría ser inestable.' Para inflamación, solo 34 participantes verificados en 2 estudios humanos respaldan una calificación Moderada. Un único ensayo grande u atípico podría cambiar la dirección agrupada; a la inversa, cualquier estimación resumida es altamente sensible a qué estudios fueron recuperados.

concerns.issue: Sin efecto agrupado extraíble, lo que impide precisión metaanalítica
concerns.detail: En los cuatro resultados, el motor reporta 'ninguno extraíble' para el efecto agrupado. Esto significa que los resúmenes recuperados no proporcionan suficiente detalle (tamaños de efecto, intervalos de confianza, o datos crudos) para conducir o verificar un metanálisis. Las calificaciones se basan así en evaluación cualitativa del diseño de estudio y tamaño de muestra, no síntesis cuantitativa—un estándar de evidencia más bajo que un metanálisis robusto con análisis de sensibilidad.

concerns.issue: Una única revisión sistemática respalda dos calificaciones de resultado separadas
concerns.detail: La revisión sistemática de 2022 (n=10) aparece en ambas bases de evidencia de desempeño del ejercicio e inflamación. Una única revisión, incluso si es de alta calidad, no puede verificar independientemente la consistencia entre resultados. Si esa revisión tiene defectos metodológicos o sesgo de publicación, ambas calificaciones se ven comprometidas. La revisión de ejercicio de 2023 (n=263) también es una revisión sistemática, no un ensayo clínico aleatorizado independiente, por lo que la evidencia humana de ejercicio se basa en síntesis secundaria de ensayos primarios de calidad individual desconocida.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Los estudios en animales sugieren que Rhodiola puede modular marcadores inflamatorios (citoquinas, corticosterona) y vías anti-fatiga, lo que conecta plausiblemente con ansiedad reducida y mayor resiliencia del ejercicio. Sin embargo, hay un salto sustancial de cambios de biomarcadores en roedores a resultados clínicos humanos: la evidencia de estrés/ansiedad humana es un único ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2015 (tamaño de muestra desconocido), y la evidencia de desempeño del ejercicio conflúe revisiones sistemáticas con un pequeño ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2025. El mecanismo es biológicamente coherente, pero la evidencia clínica humana es demasiado escasa y opaca para confirmar si la vía se traduce en beneficio humano significativo.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que 4 de 6 estudios de inflamación y 2 de 3 estudios de estrés/ansiedad son modelos animales, que frecuentemente fallan en traducirse a eficacia humana. El único ensayo clínico aleatorizado en humanos sobre estrés/ansiedad (2015) tiene 11 años de antigüedad, es insuficientemente potenciado por estándares modernos, y no tiene tamaño de muestra reportado en el resumen—podría ser un piloto pequeño. Para desempeño del ejercicio, la evidencia se basa en revisiones sistemáticas (síntesis secundaria, no ensayos independientes) y un único ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2025 con 96 participantes con una combinación no probada (Rhodiola + cafeína), lo que hace poco claro cuál agente, si acaso alguno, es responsable. La ausencia de estimaciones de efecto agrupadas en todos los resultados sugiere heterogeneidad o datos primarios de baja calidad, consistente con un efecto nulo o trivial enmascarado por sesgo de publicación.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Ensayos clínicos aleatorizados preregistrados, adecuadamente potenciados (n≥150 por brazo) en humanos en resultados únicos (ej., VO₂máx en atletas de resistencia, cortisol en ansiedad clínica) con informes transparentes del tamaño de muestra, tamaños de efecto, e intervalos de confianza permitirían síntesis metaanalítica apropiada y detección de sesgo de publicación. Una replicación humana directa del ensayo de estrés/ansiedad de 2015 con metodología moderna establecería si ese hallazgo es reproducible.
